name: Burgruine Kropfsberg
kurzbeschreibung: The Kropfsberg Castle Ruin near Brixlegg: mighty three-tower fortress of the Archbishops of Salzburg from the 13th century at the intersection of the Inn Valley and Ziller Valley.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Kropfsberg Castle Ruin is perched on a prominent wooded rocky outcrop above the Inn Valley community of Reith im Alpbachtal, precisely at the strategically important intersection between the Inn Valley and the entrance to the Ziller Valley. Built in the early 13th century by the powerful Archbishops of Salzburg as a formidable border fortress against the Counts of Tyrol, the castle complex quickly developed into one of the largest defensive structures in the entire Alpine region by area. With its former three fortified keeps, deep neck ditches, and extensive curtain walls, it was for centuries the scene of armed conflicts, historical peace negotiations, and princely jurisdiction throughout the Lower Inn Valley, also securing lucrative customs revenues along the historic trade routes.

Route & Requirements

From the sunny valley floor of the community of Reith, a picturesque, well-marked, and family-friendly forest hiking trail leads up to the historic ruin complex with a gentle, steady incline. The pure walking time from the parking lot at the valley bottom is only twenty to thirty minutes and requires no alpine mountain experience or excessive fitness. Once at the top, secured circular paths invite visitors to safely explore the massive walls, the preserved gate tower, and the foundations of the medieval palas. Sturdy, comfortable leisure footwear is recommended to ensure a secure and non-slip grip on the natural gravel paths and grassy areas.

Visit & Arrival

The exterior areas of the ruin are freely accessible during the day all year round; in the restored inner courtyard, atmospheric cultural evenings, medieval festivals, atmospheric open-air theater performances, and exciting historical castle tours for history enthusiasts occasionally take place during the summer months. Arrival by car is via the Inntalautobahn A12 to the Kramsach/Wiesing exit and then on the state road to the designated hiking parking lot directly at the foot of the castle hill. Train travelers can take the regional train to Brixlegg station, from where an idyllic footpath along the Inn Valley cycle path leads to the start of the castle ascent in about twenty minutes.

Tips

The exposed location of the former Salzburg fortress offers a fantastic panoramic view of the Ziller Valley, the Lower Inn Valley, and the rugged rock formations of the Rofan Mountains. Combine your visit with a detour to the neighboring flower village of Reith im Alpbachtal or combine the castle visit with an easy bike tour along the Inn Cycle Path. Especially in the late afternoon hours, the low sun bathes the ancient masonry in an incomparably warm light, creating ideal conditions for atmospheric photo opportunities.
